rows.subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
rows.description: A toy car stops making its noise, so a toddler carries it to father, holds it up and says "no." The caregiver is treated as the repair service.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit

rows.description: A toddler has seen mother call "Dadi!" when something breaks. Now a shoe strap comes loose and the toddler shouts "Dadi" toward the next room.
A toddler shakes the silent toy, bangs it on the floor and presses the button several times. Only after none of it works does the toddler set off to find mother.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit

rows.description: A teddy is wedged behind the sofa and a toddler screams from the spot, waiting. The caregiver hears the noise but cannot tell what is wrong, so help arrives late.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit

rows.subtype: Approach: leading the caregiver by hand [Revision]
rows.description: Mother says "wait a minute," so the toddler grabs her finger and pulls her to the sofa, pointing at the teddy. Bringing the adult to the problem fixes the missing message.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit

rows.description: The wedged teddy will not come out, so a toddler stops trying, walks away and does not tell anyone. The toy stays lost until a caregiver finds it later.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit

rows.subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
rows.description: A toddler brings an empty katori to mother and taps it, saying "aur." Handing over the bowl says more than the word does.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, trial and error

rows.description: A toddler tugs at the kitchen cupboard where biscuits are kept, then at the fridge handle, then points at the counter. Each try shows what can be reached.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, delegation

rows.description: At mealtime a toddler copies the family, saying "roti" and holding out both hands. The word, learned by copying, is treated as a way to make food appear.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: delegation, trial and error

rows.description: Rubbing the tummy and saying "num" once made grandmother bring milk. A toddler now rubs the belly whenever hungry, whether or not anyone is looking.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, delegation, trial and error
